question: What would I tell the Commercial Director?
answer:
Here is the briefing, all figures as of 4 September 2026 covering 6 August to 4 September across the pilot regions.

The headline is that the estate publishes 99.26% reported reliability, which is status-derived uptime, while delivered reliability, the share of driver charging attempts that actually transferred energy, is 95.29%. That is a gap of 3.96 percentage points. The two use different denominators and are not two versions of the same measure: the gap is where status-based monitoring overstates what drivers experienced.

Be careful how the gap is characterised externally. Of the 4.71 point delivered failure rate, 4.30 points are diffuse baseline failure spread thinly across the estate (declines, handshake errors, drivers giving up) and cannot be fixed by dispatching an engineer. Only 0.40 points sit on the 26 chargers the detector flagged. That is the actionable share, and it accounts for 677 of the 7,901 failed attempts.

The commercially interesting finding is the monitoring blind spot. There are 123 open alerts across 106 devices, and 26 detected silent failures, with an overlap of zero: none of the silently failing chargers appear in the alert queue, because the existing rules watch the fault log and these units report themselves healthy. Estimated hidden revenue at risk on those 26 is £12,648.95 for the observed period, with an ongoing daily loss rate of £707.92 across the 3 episodes still running. Treat these as prioritisation estimates, not accounting-grade lost revenue.

For the first engineer, the list ranked by dispatch priority (still-running episodes first, then daily loss rate) puts CHG-0034 at Birmingham Motorway 006 top: 100% reported uptime, 0% delivered success, 63 of 63 attempts failed since 2 September against same-site peers at 95.75%, £383.75 a day. Two caveats worth stating in the room: detection is deliberately conservative, so short or low-traffic episodes are missed, and this pilot data is synthetic, so nothing here is a finding about the live estate.

metric_definitions.reliability_gap_points: reported_reliability_percent minus delivered_reliability_percent, in percentage points. NOT the failure rate - the two differ by the downtime that status reporting already captures.
metric_definitions.delivered_failure_rate_points: Share of attempts that failed, in percentage points. Equals reliability_gap_points plus reported_downtime_points.
metric_definitions.failure_points_from_detected_devices: Portion of the delivered failure rate attributable to chargers the detector flagged. This is the actionable part.
metric_definitions.failure_points_baseline_diffuse: Portion of the delivered failure rate spread thinly across the estate - declines, handshake failures, drivers giving up. Not fixable by dispatching an engineer.

assumptions: The gap equals the delivered failure rate minus the downtime that status reporting already captures.
Failures on detected devices are treated as the actionable share; everything else is diffuse baseline failure.
caveats: The decomposition splits the FAILURE RATE, not the gap. Failure rate minus reported downtime equals the gap.
Baseline failures - declines, handshake errors, drivers giving up - are not fixable by dispatching an engineer.

metric_definitions.visible_alert_count: Alerts currently open in the operations queue.
metric_definitions.silent_failure_count: Chargers the detector flagged as impaired while status reporting shows them healthy.
metric_definitions.alert_silent_overlap: How many detected silent failures also appear in the alert queue. Zero is the finding: none of them do.
metric_definitions.hidden_revenue_at_risk: Total estimated revenue at risk across detected silent failures for the observed period. An estimate for operational prioritisation, not an accounting-grade lost-revenue figure.

assumptions: The existing alert rules watch the fault log, so they can only surface conditions that produced a fault.
Detected silent failures are units whose delivered performance is materially below same-site peers while status reporting shows them operational.
caveats: This is an estimate for operational prioritisation, not an accounting-grade lost-revenue calculation.

Inspect the affected connector - unit appears available on the other outlet
Investigate session drop-outs - sessions start then terminate early
Dispatch engineer - physical inspection, unit reports available but delivers nothing
Investigate power delivery - sessions succeed but well below rated output

metric_definitions.silent_failure_count: Chargers the detector flagged as impaired while status reporting shows them healthy.
metric_definitions.estimated_revenue_at_risk_gbp: Estimate for operational prioritisation, not an accounting-grade lost-revenue calculation.
metric_definitions.daily_loss_rate_gbp: no description published in the semantic layer
metric_definitions.dispatch_priority: Triage order. Episodes still running rank first, then by daily loss rate - you dispatch on what is still bleeding, not on sunk cost.

assumptions: A charger is flagged only if its delivered success is materially below same-site peers over the same window while status reporting shows it operational.
Dispatch priority puts episodes that are still running first, then ranks by daily loss rate - you dispatch on what is still bleeding, not on what has already been lost.
caveats: This is an estimate for operational prioritisation, not an accounting-grade lost-revenue calculation.
Detection is deliberately conservative. Short or low-traffic episodes fall below the thresholds and will be missed.
